=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- File: scripts/review_commit_changes.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 175-190 (the `changelog.d/*.md` case arm)
  Problem: The bash case pattern `changelog.d/*.md` uses a bare glob star, which in bash case statements matches any characters including path separators. The pattern will therefore preserve markdown files at any depth under `changelog.d/`, not only top-level fragments. This is inconsistent with the stated intent ("only `*.md` under `changelog.d/` survives; any other new file — including a non-`.md` stray inside `changelog.d/` — is still removed"), and with the pattern style used by the adjacent exemption `scripts/*|prompts/*` which uses the directory-prefix form rather than a trailing glob.
  Why it fails at runtime: A future stray `changelog.d/notes/foo.md` (a non-top-level markdown artifact) would be preserved when the intent of the tight-scope fix is to exempt only top-level fragments written by the editor. While no pipeline artifact writes to nested changelog.d paths today, the pattern inconsistency creates a latent over-preservation surface that could surprise future maintainers.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

- File: scripts/review_commit_changes.sh:178
  Line or code reference: `changelog.d/*.md)` (bash `case` glob)
  Problem: The glob `changelog.d/*.md` only matches files directly under `changelog.d/`. A reviewer-created fragment placed in a subdirectory (`changelog.d/sub/dir/fragment.md`) would still be removed by the consumer cleanup path.
  Why it fails at runtime: The editor (or a future change that nests fragments) would produce a file that is deleted before staging, re-triggering the exact `EDITOR_CHANGES_LOST` dead-end the PR was meant to eliminate. The test `test_consumer_cleanup_still_removes_non_fragment_files_in_changelog_dir` only covers a sibling non-`.md` file, not deeper nesting.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/review_commit_changes.sh:185
  Line or code reference: `echo "Preserving editor-created changelog fragment: ${created_file}"`
  Problem: The log message is inaccurate for the source-repo path (where `IS_WORKFLOW_SOURCE_REPO=true` skips the entire removal block) and for any non-editor-created `.md` file that happens to match the glob.
  Why it fails at runtime: Operators debugging a consumer run see a misleading message that implies editor involvement even when the file was pre-existing or the run is on the workflow-source repo. No functional breakage, but violates operational clarity (unattended_system_instructions.md §4, AGENTS.md repo hygiene).
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: tests/test_review_commit_changelog_fragment_preserved.py:67-72
  Line or code reference: `assert "changelog.d" not in m.group(1)` (staging-pathspec test)
  Problem: The test only asserts absence of the literal string `"changelog.d"` in the pathspec. It would still pass if the pathspec were changed to something broader that still contained `"changelog.d"` (e.g. `changelog.d/**/*.md` or a negated glob that accidentally matched). The regex extraction for the cleanup block is also brittle (relies on a large DOTALL match that could break on unrelated comment or whitespace changes).
  Why it fails at runtime: A future maintainer could broaden the glob or alter the staging command without the test catching the regression, re-introducing the fragment-deletion bug for nested fragments or breaking consumer staging.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
